summary: Two steel range towers of 1900 at the upper entrance to the Lachine Canal in Parc Saint-Louis; keepers from 1849; federal heritage buildings since 1991; still listed by the Coast Guard.

light.note: Front light focal height 9.4 m; rear light focal height 17.9 m (CCG 2025, column 'focal height in metres above water'). Both nominal range 12 nm.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Front light on a wharf with paid parking.

events.note: Wooden pier light at the canal's western entrance, per LighthouseFriends (front page). The 1849 date is from LighthouseFriends, which cites the Commissioners of Public Works.
Two new pole lights added at Lachine; keeper's pay raised $50 for keeping them.
Present steel range towers, built for the Department of Railways and Canals; transferred to the Department of Marine in 1902 (1903 report).
Equipment platform erected above the rear tower's cupola.
Both towers designated Recognized Federal Heritage Buildings.

keepers.name: John Norton
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends' history says he was made keeper of Lachine Lighthouse (the paragraph follows the 1849 pier light, no year stated); its head-keeper list prints 'at least 1851 - 1880'. Superannuated at 78 in 1880; died later that year.

keepers.name: Charles Leger
keepers.note: Salary $200 a year at appointment; raised $50 in 1889 for the two pole lights.

keepers.name: Alphonse Blondin
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends prints his head-keeper span as 1891 to 1896; dismissed in 1897 after an investigation found he had farmed out the keeping of two lights.

keepers.name: Arthur Lizotte
keepers.note: The 1914 keepers' table (Marine report for the fiscal year ended 31 March 1914, printed 1915, p. 66) lists 'Lachine ranges' / 'A. Lizotte, Jr' / appointed April 27, 1910 / salary 305.00. Checked against the page image (scan p. 73): row confirmed, date read as 27 April 1910 from the image (OCR reads 'Ai^ril').

keepers.name: Eugunie Malo
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends prints 'Eugunie Malo' (1921-1923) and is the only source read for her; no sex, first name variant or Marine-report record is shown. Not found in the Marine reports read (corpus grep 'Eugunie' returned nothing). Spelling and identity unverified. Story does not describe her sex.

corrections.why: The record's 1889 date is the year two pole lights were added at Lachine. The pier light at the canal's western entrance dates from 1849, and the present range towers date from 1900. Source is LighthouseFriends, which cites the Commissioners of Public Works (1850 report). That report is not in the corpus, so the 1849 date is single-sourced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record and LighthouseFriends disagree on whether the range lights are still lit. The Coast Guard's March 2025 List of Lights still lists both lights (F G, seasonal, night only), so they are shown as active in the story. The record's '2025 deactivated' event is not supported by any source read.

notes_for_editor: Record conflicts. (1) Lit status: the record's 'status active' and '2025 deactivated' do not match. The March 2025 Coast Guard list still shows both ranges (F G, seasonal, night only); the story follows the list. A later notice may exist that the sources read do not show. (2) first_lit: the record's 1889 is the pole-light year, not the pier light (1849, LighthouseFriends). The rear range distance: LighthouseFriends' 1903 report figure is 904 ft from the front light; the 2025 list gives 250.6 m, so the rear light's position may have been re-surveyed. Not used. (3) Heights: the 2025 list gives front 9.4 m and rear 17.9 m (focal height above water); LighthouseFriends gives 30 ft and 44 ft above the lake's summer level (1903 report). The list's figures are used. (4) Keepers: LighthouseFriends' head keeper list is the roster. The 1914 keepers' table 'A. Lizotte, Jr' was matched by row position on the OCR and confirmed on the page image (scan p. 73, printed p. 66); the date and salary (27 April 1910; 305.00) were read from the image. 'Eugunie' Malo (1921-1923) is spelled as LighthouseFriends prints it, is not in the Marine reports read, and is not described as a woman in any source; the story says nothing about her sex. John Norton's span is 'at least 1851' per LighthouseFriends' head-keeper list; the story says the start date is not fixed. (5) The 1849 pier light and the 1889 poles come only from LighthouseFriends; the 1850 Commissioners' report is not in the corpus. (6) The 1900 replacement is confirmed by the Marine report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1903 (volume printed 1904). The 'Department's 1903 description' is labelled by that fiscal year end, not calendar 1903. (7) The towers' shape: heritage sources say truncated cone; the 2025 list calls the tower 'cylindrical'. Not resolved; the story uses the heritage description. (8) No Montreal newspaper search was run; Chronicling America does not cover these Montreal papers. Nothing sourced on automation date or on when the last resident keeper left.
